lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹176 cr vs working capital ₹5,810 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years

ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +51%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings

story.what_it_does: MRF sells tyres and related products, and its sales crossed Rs 30,000 crore in FY2025-26. It also exports, and buys some raw materials from a related party, MRF SG PTE LTD.
story.plans: Management plans further price hikes and cost cuts to offset rising raw material costs. It says tyre demand should stay strong, but gives no numbers, and the notes show no capex or capacity plans.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a moat directly. Strong demand, new product launches and the ability to raise prices hint at some brand and pricing strength, though market share and margin data are not disclosed.

scenarios.story: Demand stays good, helped by lower GST rates and new launches, and price hikes plus cost cuts fully offset higher raw material costs. Profit then resumes growing, as it did in FY2025-26 when consolidated net profit rose 30%.
signals_to_watch: Total income keeps growing year on year, as it did in April-June 2026 (Rs 8610.56 crore vs Rs 7804.23 crore)
Management says the cost pressure on margins is easing

scenarios.story: Sales keep rising on good demand, but costs stay firm because of the ongoing conflict. Price hikes only partly offset them, so profit stays roughly flat, as in April-June 2026.
signals_to_watch: Net profit versus the prior-year quarter (Rs 495.35 crore vs Rs 501.82 crore in April-June)
Management comments that higher costs will continue to affect margins

scenarios.story: Raw material costs and supply disruption from the Middle East conflict rise further, and price hikes cannot keep up. A sub-normal monsoon and geopolitical headwinds on exports could also weaken demand.
signals_to_watch: Profit before tax falling further below the prior-year level (Rs 649.69 crore vs Rs 671.83 crore)
Sub-normal monsoon hurting demand, or export growth held back by geopolitical headwinds
